historical_reviews.deepseek: The literal range cannot prove four resources, the fallback may omit members, and the retimer-temperature oracle is unrelated.

historical_reviews.v3_1: Expected fan count follows actual approved PSU population and per-PSU fan architecture; PSU slot identity, presence and redundancy state must accompany RPM so an absent supply is not misread as a failed fan.

original_test_intent: Verify that BMC Web correctly represents every expected PSU1 through PSU4 fan resource, including slot/fan identity, RPM or reading, units, health, thresholds, freshness, population and redundancy context against the approved SPEC.
original_method: Establish target PSU population and redundancy topology; enumerate explicit fan resources in the protected Web UI; capture filters, pagination and refresh; bind each row to a physical PSU slot/fan; compare fields and range to the SPEC; optionally correlate full backend data; preserve logs and do not change fan or power policy.
manual_activity: A platform reviewer confirms expected PSU population, slot/fan/redundancy mapping and all rendered fan rows against the approved power/cooling SPEC.
required_inputs: Approved PSU population and slot map
safety_requirements: Do not alter fan curves/duty, PSU state, redundancy, power or firmware
Distinguish absent PSU from failed fan
agent_execution_scope: Capture UI context and complete rows
Map every member to slot/fan and presence state
Compare RPM, units, health, thresholds, timestamp and range
engineer_actions: Approve PSU population, redundancy and fan matrix
Visually confirm all expected UI rows
Resolve absent, duplicate, stale or ambiguous fans

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The literal `PSU1~4_FAN` read does not enumerate per-slot resources, `head -100` can omit them, and RTM temperature output is unrelated.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Enumerate exact UI members based on populated PSU slots; use full untruncated per-member backend reads only as approved same-data cross-checks.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The Web/SPEC check and 3/3-minute estimate remain; generic clearing and retimer substitution are excluded.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Join PSU inventory/presence and redundancy state to every fan row before assessing RPM, status, thresholds and range.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds physical slot population and redundancy semantics to the generic sensor check.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A missing fan sensor may mean an absent PSU, mapping defect or failure; RPM alone cannot distinguish them.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Some PSU models expose multiple internal fans or aggregate speed; the project SPEC must define the authoritative per-slot model.

project_override_considerations: Define which PSU slots are populated, how many fan resources each supply exposes and acceptable redundancy/RPM state. Duplicate retimer coverage stays separate; backend-only substitution needs approved UI equivalence.
expected_evidence: Target/firmware/Web route and PSU inventory/redundancy map
Protected UI captures for every expected PSU fan with page context
Per-slot presence/fan identity, RPM, units, health, thresholds, timestamp and range result
No-fan/no-power-mutation and no-log-clear audit plus engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Web procedure and SPEC criterion target PSU fans consistently. Generic clearing and DeepSeek's retimer oracle are method/reference defects.

blocked_analysis.analysis: PSU population, redundancy, fan SPEC and protected UI are obtainable package inputs; execution becomes BLOCKED only if the expected fan model remains indeterminate.

review_improvement: Makes absence, slot identity and redundancy first-class evidence so a literal range or unrelated retimer temperature cannot pass the PSU cooling check.
independent_technical_reasoning: PSU fan telemetry is conditional on supply presence and internal fan architecture. A zero or missing RPM has different meaning for an absent slot, standby supply and installed failed fan; valid acceptance therefore requires the inventory/redundancy state and physical slot binding before interpreting each sensor.
